fields: Without answer choices, what is the best architecture response to this scenario? A support assistant only needs order lookup and refund-request submission, but it has a production database admin credential. What should change first?
Replace the broad credential/tool with scoped capabilities needed for those tasks. Reduce unnecessary capability and blast radius rather than relying on instructions.
Resolve this production scenario for tool and agent capability bloat: A coding agent legitimately needs shell access. What is the strongest architecture?
Allow the broad tool inside a constrained sandbox with scoped credentials and permissions. General-purpose capability can be valid when strong containment limits reach and impact.

What should an architect recommend in this tool and agent capability bloat situation? An agent has twelve overlapping CRM tools with vague names and often chooses the wrong one. What is the best improvement?
Reduce overlap and define clearer, distinct tool boundaries and descriptions. Overlapping capability increases selection ambiguity.
State the preferred architecture action for this design-review scenario: Which change most directly reduces the blast radius of a read-only reporting agent?
Remove write credentials and destructive tool operations it does not need. Hard capability restriction reduces what can happen if the model is wrong or compromised.
Capability bloat — D3.1 application
Exposing more tools, data, credentials, or side effects than the task needs.
Least privilege — D3.1 application
Granting only the minimum capability required to perform the task.
blast radius — D3.1 application

Resolve this production scenario for authentication and authorization: An MCP tool is protected by OAuth. Where should access be checked?
At the protected protocol/application boundary using verified authorization context. Authorization is an enforceable control outside model output.
What should an architect recommend in this authentication and authorization situation? A SaaS agent uses one backend superuser credential for every tenant. What is the primary risk?
A failure in model/tool logic can cross tenant boundaries because the execution identity is overprivileged. Shared broad credentials defeat least-privilege and tenant isolation.
State the preferred architecture action for this design-review scenario: A consequential tool call occurs after initial login. What is the safest design?

Without answer choices, what is the best architecture response to this scenario? A reranker improves grounded accuracy by 0.3% but adds 1.5 seconds to a 2-second SLA. What should the architect do?
Evaluate whether the small quality gain justifies violating or consuming most of the latency budget. Accuracy and latency are explicit trade-offs against workload constraints.
Resolve this production scenario for accuracy-latency trade-offs: Four retrieval calls use unrelated sources and do not depend on one another. How can wall-clock time often be reduced?
Run the independent calls in parallel and combine results. Independent work is a good candidate for parallel execution.
What should an architect recommend in this accuracy-latency trade-offs situation? A system is slow. Retrieval is 50 ms, model inference 2.8 s, and formatting 20 ms. Where should optimization start?
The dominant model-inference contribution, subject to quality constraints. Optimize the dominant contributor rather than the easiest component.
State the preferred architecture action for this design-review scenario: Tool Search reduces context and wrong-tool calls but adds a lookup step. When is it most justified?
When the accuracy/context benefit outweighs the added lookup latency for the workload. Progressive discovery itself has a trade-off and should be evaluated.
Latency budget — D3.3 application
The portion of end-to-end response time available to system stages under the SLA.

Executing independent operations concurrently to reduce wall-clock time.
